title: Grade the Content
tag: One classroom move, under three minutes, for the teacher who teaches content, not English.

a: Grade the Content, Grow the English
beats.say: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move six: grade the content, grow the English.

chunks.text: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move six: grade the content, grow the English.

a: “The water it was boil at 100 degree. The temperature it no change when we add more heat because the energy go to make the gas.”
beats.say: Here is a real kind of lab conclusion from a level-two student. The water it was boil at one hundred degree. The temperature it no change when we add more heat because the energy go to make the gas.

chunks.text: Here is a real kind of lab conclusion from a level-two student.
The water it was boil at one hundred degree.
The temperature it no change when we add more heat because the energy go to make the gas.

beats.say: What grade does that get? In a lot of classrooms, a sixty. Spelling, verbs, articles — it bleeds red. And the student who gets a sixty for that will quit on you by October, and then you've lost the chemistry too.

a: Temperature stays constant during a phase change ✓
beats.say: Look again. Read it as a chemist. Water boils at one hundred degrees. The temperature stays constant during the phase change. The added energy goes into making the gas. That is a correct explanation of latent heat. Every point. The English is a level two. Those are two different things.

a: Row 1 · Content: did they get the science right? → grade this fully
beats.say: Row one: content. Did they get the science right? Grade that fully. This conclusion is full credit for science.

a: Row 2 · Language: note it, feedback on ONE thing, don't let it sink the grade
beats.say: Row two: language. Note it. Give feedback on one thing. Don't let it sink the grade.

chunks.text: Row two: language. Note it. Give feedback on one thing. Don't let it sink the grade.

a: This week: past tense · boil → boiled, go → went
Say it, don't just circle it
Write the correct sentence above theirs
Next week: a different one thing
beats.say: This week the one thing is past tense. Boil, boiled. Go, went. Say it to the student in person; don't just circle it — a circle says you're wrong, the corrected sentence says here's how it goes. Write the correct sentence above theirs. Next week, a different one thing. The rest will come.

a: Accommodation: how they show it — extra time, word bank, dictionary, read aloud, draw instead of write
Modification: a lower standard — not for ELs unless an IEP says so
beats.say: And keep the distinction straight. An accommodation changes how a student shows what they know: extra time, a word bank, a bilingual dictionary, the question read aloud, a drawing instead of a paragraph. The standard stays the same. A modification lowers the standard. English learners get accommodations, not modifications — and the ones your student gets are written in their Language Service Plan. Get a copy.

beats.say: A student who gets a ninety-five for the science and a note about the verbs comes back tomorrow and writes more. That's how the English grows: by writing, a lot, without fear, with one thing fixed at a time.
